How to write a comparative essay?

Tagged: Essay Writing

Share this:

  • Facebook
  • Twitter
  • LinkedIn
A comparative essay is composed of several paragraphs that attempt to explain how two issues are either similar or different from one another. In these pieces, contrasting and comparing various aspects of the subjects under discussion is a major focus.

1. Determine the comparison's basis.

You must provide a foundation for comparison based on the question. The inquiry often provides the basis for comparison. There are times, nevertheless, when the writer has to elaborate on the same.

  • You can be asked to contrast capitalism with communism as an example of a comparison essay. You don't need to go above and above because the question's objective is obvious.
  • To analyse any political beliefs is still another cause. In order to answer this broad topic, you must identify the various political philosophies. Identify any you can compare after that. In these circumstances, the writer must expand the foundation of comparison on their own.

2. Develop the essay's content.

This process is deciding what will be included while writing essay. It involves identifying the differences and similarities between the things under comparison. It is necessary to elaborate on the ways in which the issues are similar and how they are different. You may develop your initial strategy on how to write a comparative essay by using this listing. In order to adequately analyse the main points of comparison for the essay, the listing should be carefully evaluated. The areas that could be connected must be the main emphasis. Additionally, the ones that may be far less significant have to be cancelled.

3. Create a thesis

An essay's thesis statement should be crystal clear and serve as the writer's guidance. It doesn't matter if the question specifies the comparative basis or if the author has identified it. You must first look at the list including the several aspects of comparison in order to provide you the thesis statement. Determine if the subjects are more similar or significantly different, and decide accordingly. You may create a simple thesis statement for a comparison essay based on this assessment. The similarities and differences between the subjects must be reflected in this thesis statement. In such situations, the essay thesis must draw attention to both the themes' similarities and distinctions without losing sight of either.

4. Make the essay's structure clear.

For individuals who lack the knowledge necessary to compose a comparative essay, essays have unique Guidelines and structures. So an essay that compares two things is not an exception. Due to the fact that it should be written so that the reader can easily follow the comparisons made in the essay. The main ways that a comparison essay might be organised are as follows.

Alternating Method

In this method, treat the subject of comparison in a single paragraph. This shows that a full paragraph is used to thoroughly discuss one point of comparison in connection to the main issue. The next paragraph will then explicitly describe the same thing in every other paragraph while adding the second subject. This is just to point out that the second paragraph and the first paragraph explain the same comparison. But there are offers for the first and second circumstances, respectively. This implies that every other feature may be covered in the third and fourth paragraphs, nonetheless, with respect to the first and second topics. If you still don't understand how to create a comparative essay, this series continues till the conclusion.

Advantages

1. Provides more details about the thing than is typical, making it simple to deal with specific topics

2. Creates a fully researched and written paper.

When to use this method

1. Situations requiring a distinct comparison
2. When the contrasted elements are unrelated

Mixed paragraphs method

Here, a single paragraph is devoted to describing how the topics compare depending on that particular issue. In this manner, the first problem is dealt with first, followed by the second, and so on.

Advantages

1. equalises the weights assigned to the subjects in terms of contrast
2. The reader is able to quickly recognise the comparison element

When to use this method

1. Managing a lengthy comparison essay
2. Or when dealing with intricate issues that demand careful consideration

Block Method

Despite being extremely risky, this is actually the greatest course of action. Divide the text into sections—that is the essential idea here. One topic is covered in the first component, while another circumstance is covered in the second component. In this manner, the initial section of the comparison includes definitions of subject one and all of the relevant comparison elements. The second section then deals with the ideal circumstance. You must be motivated to learn how to write a comparative essay, though. To enable easy following and related, make sure the second portion precisely follows the first section's order.

  • When managing a brief essay
  • Or when addressing simple topics
  • Situations when the comparison elements for topic one and subject two don't clearly relate to one another
  • When you need to develop the concepts for the circumstance, start with those from topic one that were highlighted.
  • When managing multiple topics
